title: Model extensible workflow state as an algebraic union
summary: A named Union makes workflow alternatives explicit and lets exhaustive decisions expose new cases.
recommendation: When a stateful workflow can grow beyond a genuinely binary condition, model its alternatives as a named Union and use exhaustive transitions.
rationale: Boolean flags and independent fields can hide impossible combinations; a tagged union keeps each meaningful state visible to readers and analyzers.
exceptions: Keep a Boolean for a stable, genuinely binary condition.
A large Union can be clearer than an artificial decomposition when its alternatives are intrinsically coupled.
confidence: The rule sees only state-named Boolean fields and state-named unions with eight or more alternatives. A Boolean can be correct and a large union can be appropriate.

lint_rule.source_text:
use language (
  version is v0.1,
  features is ( lint )
)
# The host supplies two bounded syntax facts: a state-named Boolean field and a
# state-named Union with eight or more alternatives. Either fact asks for an
# advisory. It cannot prove that a Boolean is wrong or that a large union is
# unmaintainable.
rule is fn static (boolean-state : Boolean, large-union : Boolean) -> Boolean
  (not boolean-state) and (not large-union)
